title: Not a quiet place: Validating C‐ and F‐PODs to predict harbor porpoise presence in the Ems estuary
content:
Abstract

Shifting from cetacean porpoise detectors (C-POD) to full waveform capture porpoise detectors (F-POD) poses the question as to which device detects more harbor porpoises' echolocations and offers a higher level of precision and accuracy and a lower validation effort. C- and F-PODs were deployed together in the Ems estuary at the German–Dutch border during their spring peak presence (February–June 2023). Detections were validated visually, and ecological models were parametrized for “NBHF” (narrow band high frequency, unvalidated) and “verified” data (validated) to showcase the risk of ignoring bias. Time-aggregated porpoise detections were significantly lower in C- than in F-PODs (1,644 vs. 2601 min; 1,094 vs. 1,301 10-min intervals). Overall, C-PODs achieved a higher level of precision and accuracy (Hi and Mod setting: 0.81 and 0.96) than F-PODs (0.39 and 0.51). In F-PODs, applying filters during train processing increased the relative number of harbor porpoise click-trains and reduced validation effort. As random forest models have shown from “NBHF” and “verified” data, overestimation and underestimation led to false association of ecological variables with harbor porpoise presence and biased predictions. Hence, visual validation is required for data of both porpoise detectors to ensure unbiased ecological interpretations.
